kinds.regulation: FIA 2026 Section C text (Issue 19, in force at Silverstone; unchanged in Issue 21 unless noted)
kinds.official: FIA / F1 / team / Pirelli / supplier statement or document
kinds.reported: press, third-party simulations, forums (grade in the source's how)
kinds.derived: computed from public telemetry or regulation numbers, method in derivation
kinds.fitted: a model estimate made in this repo (sim, identify, derive-car): an effective value of that model
kinds.estimate: judgement where nothing is public, always with a range

entries.label: Power unit layout
entries.value: 1.6 L V6 at 90 deg, bore 80 mm, 4 valves/cyl, single turbo (<= 150,000 rpm), no MGU-H; only the ICE and the ERS-K may propel the car
entries.derivation: Section C Issue 19, C5.1.2-4, C5.3.1, C5.3.6, C5.2.1 (as read for redbull-2026.json)

entries.label: Geometric compression ratio (max, checked hot from 1 Jun 2026)
Fuel energy flow cap below 10,500 rpm
entries.derivation: C5.2.4; reaches 3000 MJ/h at exactly 10,500 rpm, so revs above it earn no extra fuel

entries.label: DM01 ICE crank power (>= 10,500 rpm)
entries.derivation: No Red Bull/Ford figure is public. FIA design figure for a 2026 ICE: ~400 kW. FIA ADUO period 1: Mercedes 2-4 % below the best ICE, the others > 4 % below; Sky/Auto Action name the benchmark as Red Bull Ford, so the DM01 sits at or above the field. Press estimate (ScuderiaFans, equal-drag method): Red Bull Ford 421 kW. Fitted in this repo: identify 424 +- 19 kW (prior-dominated), sim 396 kW (400 x team PU scale 0.990), derive-car 396 kW (assumed efficiency 0.475). Central 410 kW, sd 15 kW covers all of them

entries.label: ICE fuel-to-crank efficiency at full fuel flow
entries.derivation: 410 kW / 833.3 kW (pu.ice_power_peak over the C5.2.3 cap); no manufacturer has published a 2026 efficiency

entries.label: ICE power and torque vs rpm (full load)
entries.value: 0.492 x (0.27 N + 165)/3.6 kW below 10,500 rpm, 410 kW flat above
entries.derivation: regulated fuel-flow shape (C5.2.3-4) x the estimated efficiency, taken constant with rpm (no BSFC map is public; real efficiency varies with speed, so this is a smooth envelope)

entries.label: ICE crank torque at 10,500 rpm (full load)

sd_or_range.note: ~388 Nm at 6000 rpm, ~306 Nm at 12,800 rpm

entries.derivation: P/omega from pu.ice_power_curve: the C5.2.4 line gives near-constant torque below 10,500 rpm, falling as 1/N above
used_by: setup-factor work (gear ratios, roll split, heave/rake, brake bias, diff, energy map): not read by the sim yet

entries.label: Crankshaft rev limit in the rules
entries.value: none (C5.14 only bounds the spread of high rev limits to a 750 rpm band)
entries.derivation: Section C Issue 19/21 have no crank-speed cap; the 15,000 rpm in C9.8.2 is a launch-gear test speed. Press '15,000 rpm' is not in the text (REDBULL.md)

entries.label: Highest engine speed seen on Red Bull laps
entries.derivation: max of raw OpenF1 rpm over all 25 Red Bull laps (12857 VER Silverstone race; qualifying max 12808); median of the per-lap maxima 12403 rpm

entries.label: Upshift engine speed
entries.derivation: all Red Bull laps with raw samples (Q + race), consecutive-gear upshifts: midpoint of the last sample before the shift (lower bound, median 11274) and the first sample after it converted back to the old gear with the lap's own ratios (upper bound, median 12754). Fuel flow is flat above 10,500 rpm, so where in 11-12.5k the shift falls costs little

entries.label: rpm just after a downshift (braking)
entries.derivation: first raw sample after each gear decrease
used_by: setup-factor work (gear ratios, roll split, heave/rake, brake bias, diff, energy map): not read by the sim yet

entries.label: Engine speed band at full ICE power
entries.sd_or_range: lower bound exact (C5.2.4); upper bound = observed use
entries.derivation: fuel flow reaches its 3000 MJ/h cap at 10,500 rpm; Red Bull laps use up to ~12.8k

entries.label: MGU-K power (DC, deploy and harvest)
entries.sd_or_range: exact (339.5 kW mechanical at the fixed 0.97)

entries.label: MGU-K deployment limit vs speed
entries.value: min(350, 1800 - 5v) kW, 0 at >= 345 km/h (v in km/h); Overtake: 7100 - 20v, 0 at 355 km/h
entries.derivation: C5.2.8: full 350 kW to 290 km/h; 300 kW at 300, 150 kW at 330 km/h

entries.label: Recharge cap per lap (rule)
entries.derivation: C5.2.10 (lower per event; Issue 21 lowers the Q floor 5 -> 4 MJ)

entries.label: Silverstone recharge limit, SQ/Q
entries.derivation: FIA 2026 British GP Power Unit Information

entries.label: Peak superclip (full-throttle harvest) power
entries.derivation: FIA change from Miami (April 2026): 250 -> 350 kW; Silverstone (July) is after it

entries.label: ERS-K power-reduction rates (Silverstone)
entries.value: <= 150 kW step (350 kW in T1-T4, T6-T7, T15-T16, Exit T17), held 1 s, then <= 50 kW/s above 100 kW; resets Exit T1 / T9 / T17-18; speed thresholds 210 km/h (300 in T11-T14, 230 in T18)
entries.derivation: C5.12.4-C5.12.7 with the event tables (silverstone-2026-weekend.json energy_limits)

entries.label: Energy deployed on the Silverstone Q lap (DC)
entries.derivation: derive-car power balance on HAD's lap (conditional on its CdA and ICE). The physics sim's own plan deploys 8.0 MJ on the RB22 (an output, not an input). Upper bound 6.5 MJ recharge + 4 MJ window

entries.label: Where the MGU-K deploys fully (Silverstone Q)
entries.value: full 350 kW only out of slow corners onto long straights (Wellington 371, Woodcote-Copse 343, pit straight 336 kW peaks); 150-300 kW elsewhere; little after Stowe
entries.derivation: per-straight peak K_DC from the power balance (REDBULL-DERIVED.md section 2); the anchor makes the top three average 350 kW

entries.label: Clipping (speed falling at full throttle on a straight)
entries.derivation: signature: smoothed dv/dt < -0.15 m/s2 at >= 99 % throttle, < 1 g lateral, > 180 km/h, runs >= 15 m. It also contains the C5.2.8 taper above 290 km/h, Straight Mode closing, headwind and grade (no channels for those)

entries.label: Lateral friction coefficient at the static load (physical)
entries.derivation: no Pirelli figure; academic F1 tyre 1.80 at 2 kN; FIA 'minimal loss in grip' for the narrower 2026 tyre. Effective values elsewhere: sim 1.89 (inside), identify 2.27 +- 0.10, derive-car 2.54 (other estimators' scales)

entries.label: Longitudinal friction coefficient (physical)
entries.derivation: academic 1.75 at 2 kN. Effective elsewhere: sim 1.72 (inside), identify 1.49 +- 0.08, derive-car 2.09 (smoothed 3.7 Hz braking)

entries.label: Friction lost per kN of tyre load
entries.derivation: academic table 4.9-5.0 %/kN; identify's global fit sits at the top of 3-6 %/kN (0.116 per unit load ratio); sim 4.51 %/kN

entries.label: Slip angle at the lateral limit
entries.derivation: F1 tyres ~3 deg (Milliken via Wikipedia) to 8-9 deg (academic model); the sim estimates 0.098 rad inside this range

entries.label: Peak deceleration in the hardest stop of a lap (~300 km/h entry)
entries.derivation: per circuit, the Red Bull stop nearest Brembo's simulated hardest stop: raw OpenF1 speed drop over two sample intervals (~0.5 s) 4.19 g (median of 7 circuits); over one interval (~0.27 s, noisier and biased up by taking the max) 4.39 g; Brembo's simulations 3.8 g. Central 4.0 +- 0.5 g covers all three

entries.label: Peak deceleration by speed at the peak (all Q stops)
entries.sd_or_range: per band (sd = robust spread between stops)
entries.derivation: raw-sample stops with entry > 120 km/h and > 40 km/h drop; includes light stops and lifts (Becketts), so band medians sit below the hard-stop peak

entries.label: Hardest stop per circuit: Red Bull telemetry vs Brembo simulation

brembo.corner: T1 (Brembo: first corner after the line)

entries.derivation: measured brake-on time and distance come from the binary brake flag (released before the minimum), so they are shorter than Brembo's whole deceleration phase; mean_g = (entry - min) / (time to the minimum). Spa has no raw samples in the repo (no measured value)

entries.label: Brake-on time per qualifying lap
entries.derivation: sum of raw sample intervals with the brake flag on; within ~1.6 s of Brembo at Austria, Hungary, Montreal, Singapore and Monaco; Silverstone (10.2 vs 6.5 s) and Monza (10.4 vs < 8.5 s) run longer because the flag counts light dabs and trail braking outside Brembo's 3 and 5 zones

entries.label: Village (T3) stop, Red Bull laps

sd_or_range.note: the stop the sim's BRAKE_TELEMETRY (4.01 g, all 22 laps) is measured on; Red Bull laps only

entries.derivation: C11.3.3 as reported by The Drive / Brembo

entries.label: Brake system

entries.derivation: Brembo 2026 rules page

entries.label: Brake balance (front share of total braking force, friction + regen)
entries.derivation: not public. Axle loads at 4 g with h/wb 0.085 and aero balance 0.44 put the ideal front share near 0.55-0.60; rear regen (up to 350 kW, 32-40 % of peak braking power, PRIORS.md) is part of the rear share; sim uses 0.57
used_by: setup-factor work (gear ratios, roll split, heave/rake, brake bias, diff, energy map): not read by the sim yet

entries.label: Brake system capacity (deceleration cap)
entries.derivation: a cap above the tyre limit, so braking stays tyre-limited: 2025 cars reached 4.5-5 g with the same hardware class (Brembo); it does not bind in the sim

entries.label: Disc working window
entries.derivation: formula1.com: ~400 C effective, oxidises beyond 800; Silverstone brake demand index 1/5 (Brembo), so ducts can run small there
used_by: setup-factor work (gear ratios, roll split, heave/rake, brake bias, diff, energy map): not read by the sim yet

entries.label: Full-throttle acceleration by speed (Q laps, < 1 g lateral)
entries.derivation: smoothed dv/dt (+-0.45 s local quadratic), >= 99 % throttle, no brake, no lift in the next 0.45 s, plausibility-masked (audit C4 limits); 9 circuits. Below 100 km/h the throttle is rarely 99 %: see acc.corner_exit

entries.label: Corner-exit acceleration, 60-160 km/h (traction-limited)
entries.derivation: >= 50 % throttle, no brake, positive dv/dt

entries.label: Wheel power vs speed at full throttle (dE/dt + drag + rolling)
entries.sd_or_range: p_kin model-free given mass; p_wheel conditional on effective CdA (+-0.15 m2 -> +-45 kW at 250 km/h)
entries.derivation: P_kin = 1.03 m a v (m = 781 kg); P_wheel = P_kin + 0.5 rho CdA v^3 + Crr m g v with CdA 1.20 (0.95 in Straight Mode zones). Peak available at the wheel: (410 + 339.5) x 0.95 = 712 kW; the 150-250 km/h p90 near 680 kW fits full ICE + near-full MGU-K, and the fall above 290 km/h follows the C5.2.8 taper and clipping

entries.label: Peak combined crank power (ICE + MGU-K mechanical)
entries.derivation: pu.ice_power_peak + 350 x 0.97; redbull.com quotes ~745 kW for 2026 cars

entries.label: Lateral acceleration at grip-limited corner minima, by speed
entries.derivation: a_y = v_min^2 max|kappa| within +-40 m, x/y smoothed over max(6 m, 0.3 s v) (concept/identify/data.js); reads ~20-40 % above an x/y-acceleration estimate (IDENTIFY.md Scale). 9 circuits, Q laps

entries.label: Lateral limit at 100 / 200 / 250 km/h (joint 9-circuit fit, same estimator)
entries.derivation: IDENTIFY.md; Red Bull is in the leading group at 200-250 km/h with Ferrari and Mercedes

entries.label: Silverstone corner minimum speed and lateral g (Red Bull Q laps, HAD + VER)
entries.sd_or_range: spread between the two laps <= 6 km/h
entries.derivation: lowest smoothed speed within +-80 m of each MultiViewer marker; ay = v_min^2 max|kappa| (+-40 m); flat = throttle >= 95 % through the marker window (a lower bound on grip)

entries.label: Corner minimum speeds and lateral g, 8 other circuits
entries.derivation: as lat.silverstone_corners

entries.label: Peak tyre loading at Silverstone (Pirelli)
entries.derivation: Pirelli 2026 Silverstone preview: 'some corners subject the tyres to forces exceeding 5G'

entries.label: Downforce area, Corner Mode (physical)
entries.derivation: sourced prior: 2022-25 references x 0.70 (FIA -30 %). The RB22 is reported low-drag and weaker in fast corners than Mercedes/Ferrari, so not above the field. Not public for any car

entries.label: Downforce area, Corner Mode (physics-sim effective)
entries.derivation: fitted.js baseline_estimate (5.32 m2 on the pole lap) x Red Bull cla_scale 0.9992. Effective: it carries the sim line's curvature scale and its tyre law, ~1.36x the physical central; compare cars through a_y(v), not ClA (SIM.md 4.2)

entries.label: Downforce area in the other two estimators
entries.derivation: each is effective for its own tyre law (identify: load-sensitive per-car mu; derive-car: no load sensitivity, so ClA trades 1:1 with mu)

entries.label: Drag area, Corner Mode (effective: includes tyre scrub and cooling)
entries.derivation: three independent fits agree: derive-car 1.23 +- 0.17 (HAD lap, 350 kW anchor), identify 1.26 +- 0.16 (9 circuits), sim 1.23 (baseline x cda_scale 1.039). All conditional on an ICE of ~395-425 kW: +21 kW of ICE moves CdA by ~+0.09

entries.label: Drag area, Straight Mode (effective)
entries.derivation: aero.cda_corner_effective - aero.straight_mode_delta_cda (0.93); sim 0.987; derive-car 0.96; identify 0.91 +- 0.13

entries.label: Drag removed by Straight Mode
entries.derivation: apparent-power step across the A3/A4 activation points on 22 Silverstone laps (REDBULL-DERIVED.md 2): the PU output does not jump, so the step is dCdA x 0.5 rho v^3

entries.label: CdA Straight / Corner
entries.derivation: simulations of a generic 2026 car: 0.82 and 0.79; derive-car 0.78; sim 0.80; identify 0.72 +- 0.08 (prior-dominated)

entries.label: ClA Straight / Corner
entries.derivation: simulations: 0.75 and 0.69 (the floor carries more of the load in Straight Mode); sim 0.719

entries.label: Aero balance (front share of downforce, Corner Mode)
entries.derivation: not separable from speed/position telemetry; worked examples 0.41-0.44; the sim fits 0.4415 on the pole lap (balance acts only through the weaker-axle limit)

entries.label: Floor share of downforce (Corner Mode)
entries.derivation: simulation 47 %, secondary reports ~60 % (PRIORS.md); sim MODEL.floor.share 0.55

entries.label: Downforce change per mm of ride height
entries.derivation: no public 2022-26 number (PRIORS.md); 2026 floors reported less ride-height sensitive than 2022-25 (The Race, Temple); sim and aeromap use 0.6

entries.label: Active aero
entries.value: front + rear flaps, two positions, <= 400 ms transition, fails to Corner Mode; RB22 rear flap rotates 'up and over' (reported 160-180 deg) from Miami

entries.label: Silverstone wing level vs the RB22's 9-circuit mean (identify trims)
entries.derivation: ClA x e^w, CdA x e^d at Silverstone: about average downforce and ~+27 % drag (the drag trim also absorbs deployment strategy); the team did not publish its wing level

entries.label: ICE power over drag area (the best-determined drag/power combination)
entries.derivation: IDENTIFY.md: speed traces cannot separate ICE power from drag; their ratio is better determined

entries.label: Static front ride height (plank to ground)
entries.derivation: not public for any 2026 car; 2026 cars reported to run higher and with more rake than 2022-25
used_by: setup-factor work (gear ratios, roll split, heave/rake, brake bias, diff, energy map): not read by the sim yet

entries.label: Static rear ride height (plank to ground)
entries.derivation: 'rear ride heights between 2025 and the high-rake era' (The Race, Jan 2026); the design layer's single 35 mm is a mid-plank value
used_by: setup-factor work (gear ratios, roll split, heave/rake, brake bias, diff, energy map): not read by the sim yet

entries.label: Rake angle
entries.derivation: (rear - front ride height) / wheelbase = 40 / 3400 mm -> 0.67 deg; 2021 high-rake cars ran ~1-1.5 deg, 2022-25 ground-effect cars near flat
used_by: setup-factor work (gear ratios, roll split, heave/rake, brake bias, diff, energy map): not read by the sim yet

entries.label: Heave stiffness (whole car, at the tyre contact)
entries.derivation: sizes ~5 mm of aero squat under ~17 kN of Corner Mode load at 300 km/h (sim MODEL.heave_n_per_mm); 2026 platforms reported less stiff than 2022-25
used_by: setup-factor work (gear ratios, roll split, heave/rake, brake bias, diff, energy map): not read by the sim yet

entries.label: Front share of total roll stiffness
entries.derivation: not public; front-biased roll stiffness keeps lateral load transfer off the rear axle (the RB22 is reported traction-strong at low speed) at the cost of front grip. The sim takes the weaker axle with no trim, so this is the lever the setup helper needs
used_by: setup-factor work (gear ratios, roll split, heave/rake, brake bias, diff, energy map): not read by the sim yet

entries.label: Suspension layout
entries.derivation: Gary Anderson after the Barcelona test
used_by: setup-factor work (gear ratios, roll split, heave/rake, brake bias, diff, energy map): not read by the sim yet

entries.label: Differential locking on throttle (exit)
entries.derivation: no public RB22 or 2026 data; F1 differentials are hydraulically controlled and drivers change entry/mid/exit settings from the wheel. More locking adds exit traction (the RB22's reported strength) and understeer
used_by: setup-factor work (gear ratios, roll split, heave/rake, brake bias, diff, energy map): not read by the sim yet

entries.label: Differential locking off throttle (entry)
entries.derivation: as above; less entry locking helps rotation; 2026 rear regen adds an entry braking torque the diff transmits
used_by: setup-factor work (gear ratios, roll split, heave/rake, brake bias, diff, energy map): not read by the sim yet

entries.label: Brake cooling demand, Silverstone
entries.value: low (Brembo difficulty index 1 of 5; 3 braking zones; 6.5 s per lap)
entries.derivation: duct size trades against drag; no public number. Silverstone needs the least brake cooling of the season
used_by: setup-factor work (gear ratios, roll split, heave/rake, brake bias, diff, energy map): not read by the sim yet

entries.label: Qualifying energy map (Silverstone)
entries.value: 6.5 MJ recharge cap + 4 MJ window; full 350 kW out of Village/Loop, Luffield and Club onto the long straights; superclip at the ends of the pit, Wellington and Hangar straights
entries.derivation: ers.deployment_pattern + ers.clipping + the C5.12 tables
used_by: setup-factor work (gear ratios, roll split, heave/rake, brake bias, diff, energy map): not read by the sim yet
